transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luca Chen (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (StableBridge CTO), Priya Raman (Lead ML Eng), Hannah Lee (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick discovery to align on StableBridge's path to first request with Redwood (PLG/self-serve) — discussing free credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private constraints (compliance/residency), and next steps for a short hosted pilot.

Topics: quickstart credits, API key provisioning, SDK examples, latency/cost tradeoffs, SOC2/SSO/KMS, pilot scope and timelines.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick intros, I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Luca is our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Daniel (StableBridge): Hey, Daniel here — CTO. We'll try not to steal too much time, appreciate it.
[00:00:18] Priya (StableBridge): Priya, lead on ML. We'll be the ones hammering the API.
[00:00:23] Hannah (StableBridge): Hannah, platform, mainly interested in ops and security.
[00:00:28] Luca (Redwood SE): Hi all — loud and clear. Today we'll focus on the quickest path for you to hit a first request and run a short pilot.
[00:00:40] Maya: Quick housekeeping: we can do hosted trial first — usually fastest — we give credits, API key, SDK snippets, sample prompts. If you have hard compliance requirements we can talk dedicated or private after.
[00:00:56] Daniel: Sounds good. High level: we're a fintech-ish flow, some PII, some transactional metadata. We care a lot about residency and audit. Timewise we want something within two weeks ideally for a technical spike. Can Redwood get us to first request that fast?
[00:01:14] Maya: Yes — that's the PLG path. Typical time-to-first-token for teams that follow the quickstart is same day to 48 hours. You'll get trial credits and a scoped quickstart doc.
[00:01:29] Priya: When you say trial credits, is that just hosted? Or could we test a dedicated node?
[00:01:36] Maya: Initial credits apply to hosted API — that's the fastest. Dedicated capacity requires a short procurement/commit conversation, but we can often provision a small reserved pool for pilots if you need predictable throughput.
[00:01:50] Hannah: From security side, what certs and KMS options do you provide? We have to show SOC2 and AES in transit, KMS/HSM for keys, and SSO with our IdP.
[00:02:01] Luca: We support SOC2 reports, SAML/SSO via SSO integration and RBAC. For keys we have KMS integrations and can discuss HSM on Private. I'll share the security whitepaper.
[00:02:14] Daniel: Great. Also curious about latency — for some user flows we need sub-150ms 95th for short responses. Is that realistic on hosted?
[00:02:25] Luca: Sub-150ms 95th is aggressive, depends on model and prompt length. For smaller open models and sequence lengths under 64 tokens it's possible in hosted regions near your users. For strict SLOs we often recommend Dedicated so you control GPU sizing and avoid noisy neighbors.
[00:02:44] Priya: Could you explain the exact difference between the Dedicated pool and Private deployment? Because ops will ask what we actually need to build.
[00:02:51] Luca: Sure — Dedicated is reserved capacity in Redwood's cloud, it's still managed by Redwood but isolated to your account; good for predictable throughput and lower latency variance. Private is a customer-controlled deployment — VPC or on-prem — for cases with strict data residency or compliance, with a private control plane option.
[00:03:08] Maya: And to add: many customers start hosted to iterate quickly, then use Dedicated for production, and Private only when legal/regulators require full isolation.
[00:03:16] Daniel: Understood. Cost-wise, what's the delta? Rough order of magnitude?
[00:03:21] Maya: Hosted is typically lowest friction and lower upfront cost; Dedicated has a monthly reserved cost plus lower per-token unit economics; Private has license and infra costs. I'll send a simple comparison table.
[00:03:35] Hannah: Ok. For the pilot we want to validate both cost and latency — ideally using our real prompt mix. Is there an easy way to run our prompt set on Redwood so you can give us an estimate?
[00:03:47] Luca: Absolutely — if you share a sample prompt trace and typical concurrency profiles we can run throughput estimates and suggest batching/quantization profiles to hit target latency and cost.
[00:03:59] Priya: We have a staircase workload — peaks at around 200 rps for a synchronous experience, average around 60 rps. Would the hosted trial be able to emulate that?
[00:04:11] Luca: For a trial, we can provision enough concurrency to simulate spikes but sustained production spikes typically need Dedicated sizing. For the estimate I'll model 200 rps with your prompt lengths.
[00:04:23] Daniel: About data retention — if we send PII to hosted, how long is it stored? We require only ephemeral storage for user content.
[00:04:30] Maya: By default we don't use customer prompt data for training and retention windows can be configured. For enterprise customers we have options to limit retention or enable customer-managed keys in Private. I'll include the exact retention language in the security doc.
[00:04:46] Hannah: And logs for audit? We need audit trails with token-level cost and request IDs for debugging.
[00:04:53] Luca: Console provides token-level breakdown and tracing hooks. We can also stream logs to your SIEM with appropriate filters.
[00:05:01] Daniel: Okay. Step me through the actual quickstart — what do our engineers do to get the first request?
[00:05:07] Maya: Step one: sign up for our developer portal, or we can provision a trial API key for you. Step two: run the SDK example (Python/Node/curl) — it's usually a few lines. Step three: hit the model endpoint with a sample prompt. We'll provide a prompt set and a quick checklist to validate latency, token counts, and a smoke test with streaming if you need streaming.
[00:05:26] Priya: How long is the onboarding checklist? Does it cover network allowlist and SSO?
[00:05:30] Maya: Yes, it covers allowlisting IP ranges, integrating SSO, and best practices for rate limits and retries. It’s about a 1–2 page checklist.
[00:05:36] Daniel: We prefer a red-teamed checklist, but that'll do. For our pilot scope — we want to test 3 user flows: short completion (50 tokens), medium (200 tokens) and a rerank path using embeddings. Any special considerations?
[00:05:48] Luca: For reranking/embeddings we recommend separate embedding endpoints; cost per embedding unit is different. Also, reranking benefits from caching and persistent KV for prompt prefixes; we'll recommend batch settings.
[00:06:00] Priya: You mentioned quantization earlier — we use some custom transformer variants. How does Redwood handle model variants and quantized runs?
[00:06:08] Luca: We support various open models and optimized quantized variants. Runtime selects kernels based on architecture and sequence length. For unusual models we'd run a short onboarding to validate performance. Sometimes there's small accuracy regression with heavy quantization — we track that in evals.
[00:06:23] Daniel: Is that something we need to do for the pilot? Or is the hosted trial preconfigured?
[00:06:29] Maya: Hosted will have common open-models preconfigured. If you need a specific model or quantization profile, we can scope a short model onboarding step during the pilot.
[00:06:37] Hannah: Network: we need private peering for reduced latency and cert validation. Do you support private connections?
[00:06:44] Luca: Yes — Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and private links. For hosted we have region endpoints, but private peering usually requires Dedicated or Private.
[00:06:54] Daniel: About observability — we need per-route dashboards and cost attribution to features. Do you expose token-level and per-feature tagging?
[00:07:02] Luca: We expose token-level cost breakdowns and you can tag requests with a route/user metadata; Console dashboards can be filtered by tag. We'll show you a demo in the pilot.
[00:07:10] Maya: Quick interjection — we've had customers who ran a short 2-week trial and then moved to a small Dedicated pool after seeing consistent latency benefits. That seems to map to what you're asking.
[00:07:20] Daniel: Good to know. What's the expected unit pricing for hosted versus dedicated roughly? I know exacts via pricing spreadsheet but a ballpark helps the internal conversation.
[00:07:29] Maya: Ballpark: hosted per-token is higher than dedicated. Dedicated has baseline monthly commitment but can halve the per-token cost depending on utilization. I'll put examples in the spreadsheet so you can model your run rate.
[00:07:42] Priya: For the pilot, can we get telemetry hooks so our monitoring picks up request IDs and latencies?
[00:07:48] Luca: Yes — request IDs are returned and we have tracing integrations (OpenTelemetry). We'll include sample traces in the quickstart.
[00:07:56] Daniel: Any gotchas to be aware of going from quickstart to production? Like prompt caching, or KV growth, that sort of ops debt?
[00:08:03] Luca: Main ops items are KV/cache sizing, batching heuristics, and tokenization differences across models. We also advise locking model versions for production rollouts and using canary traffic splits.
[00:08:16] Hannah: For RBAC, we have strict separation between dev and prod teams. Does Redwood's Console allow per-team roles?
[00:08:21] Maya: Yes — RBAC with role-based permissions and SSO provisioning. We can provision separate API keys per team with scoped permissions.
[00:08:29] Priya: Let's talk timeline: If we share prompt traces by Wednesday, how quickly can Redwood give a throughput/latency estimate?
[00:08:37] Luca: Assuming we get traces by Wednesday, I can run an initial estimate and share numbers by Friday. If we need to run an actual benchmark we might need a 48-72 hour window to run simulations.
[00:08:49] Daniel: That timeline works. For the credit allocation: is that unlimited use during the trial or capped?
[00:08:55] Maya: Trials come with a finite credit grant — enough to run a realistic pilot. If you need more we'll extend credits for the pilot phase with a short ask.
[00:09:05] Priya: Ok. A few nitty gritty questions — do you support streaming responses and function/tool-calls? We plan to do some streaming for chat-like flows.
[00:09:13] Luca: Yes — hosted supports streaming and tool-calling abstractions via the SDKs. We'll include sample code for streaming responses.
[00:09:20] Daniel: Any limitations on request size or model length? We might have longer context in some flows.
[00:09:25] Luca: Limits depend on model; many open models handle up to 4k tokens; if you need larger contexts we can discuss segmented context or specialized models.
[00:09:34] Maya: One more thing — we often recommend customers run a quick eval comparing the hosted response quality on your prompt set vs your current baseline to ensure no regressions.
[00:09:43] Priya: We'll do that. Are there any partner integrations — observability or APM — that Redwood supports out of the box?
[00:09:50] Luca: We have integrations with common APMs and can stream logs to your DataDog/Elastic stack.
[00:09:56] Daniel: Sounds good. Let's sketch the pilot scope now so we all align. I'd propose: 1) provision hosted trial API key + credits; 2) Redwood runs throughput estimate on our sample prompts; 3) 1-week hosted pilot with traffic replay for the three flows; 4) review latency/cost and decide on Dedicated sizing. Thoughts?
[00:10:18] Maya: That matches our normal playbook. Quick question: do you need dedicated SSO or IP allowlisting during the pilot?
[00:10:25] Hannah: Ideally IP allowlist for the pilot and SSO integration in parallel but not blocking.
[00:10:32] Maya: We can do IP allowlist for the API key; SSO can be staged.
[00:10:36] Priya: For the traffic replay, do you need sanitized traces or raw? We can sanitize PII but maintain timing and token counts.
[00:10:44] Daniel: We'll sanitize but keep metadata that affects routing.
[00:10:49] Luca: That's perfect — timing and token distribution are most important for throughput/latency modelling.
[00:10:56] Maya: Okay, let's lock next steps then. I'll send a pricing + credits spreadsheet and the quickstart checklist. Luca will run the throughput estimate when you send the traces. We'll target pilot kickoff the week of 2026-12-15.
[00:11:11] Daniel: Works for us. Anything else on compliance? We may need a confidentiality addendum before sending sanitized traces.
[00:11:19] Maya: We can sign an NDA/CA quickly; I'll loop legal. For the SOC2 reports I'll share the standard pack.
[00:11:26] Hannah: One last bit — if we end up going Dedicated, what's the lead time to spin up capacity?
[00:11:32] Luca: Usually a few business days to provision a small Reserved pool after contract and onboarding. For larger capacity it can be a couple of weeks depending on GPU availability.
[00:11:43] Priya: Ok. That helps.
[00:11:46] Maya: Great. Quick wrap: Action items will be in the notes. We'll follow up via email with the docs and schedule. Thanks everyone.
[00:11:58] Daniel: Thanks — appreciate the clarity.
[00:12:01] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[00:12:03] Hannah: Bye.

Notes (AI-generated summary/snippets):
- Pilot plan: hosted trial with credits, IP allowlist, 1-week traffic replay for 3 flows (short/medium/embeddings rerank)
- Security asks: SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS/HSM options, retention policy (ephemeral option)
- Operational asks: request IDs, OpenTelemetry traces, per-route cost breakdown, RBAC

End of transcript.
